- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects in next period; dampen forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model frequently overpredicts in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; apply lag correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% for each day of lag beyond 1.
- For 30-day forecasts, model shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply downward adjustment of 1–2% to align with true mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for suppressed sentiment-driven activity.
